title: Is renting really throwing money away?

scenes.text: "Renting is throwing money away." Your parents said it. But here's the math nobody shows you.
Mike buys a $400,000 house. Jake rents the same kind of house for $1,600 a month.
Mike laughs. "You're just paying your landlord's mortgage!"
But owning has its own rent. Property tax: about 1% a year. Repairs: about 1%. And interest, plus what his down payment could have earned: about 3%.
That's roughly 5% of the price, every year. $400,000 times 5%, divided by 12, is $1,667 a month he never gets back.
Jake's rent? $1,600. So who's really throwing money away?
But here's the catch. Renting only wins if Jake invests the $80,000 he didn't put down. If he spends it, Mike wins.
So save this. Home price, times 5%, divided by 12. If rent is lower than that, renting is not throwing money away.
Rent or buy? Tell me in the comments, and follow for more.

props.disclaimer: Simplified rule of thumb (the 5% rule). Your taxes, rates and market will differ. Not financial advice.
